screens_reviewed: Two scroll captures of the same route app/audit/[placeId]/[step].tsx at step 3 (Access domain): 08-audit-domain.png (top: step header, step pills, section intro, first question) and 09-audit-domain-questions.png (mid-list: condition follow-up plus three more SelectionButton question cards, ending at the fixed footer nav).
verdict: The Access step renders as a single narrow content column on a large Android tablet canvas, with no multi-column, list/detail, or grid use even though the codebase has a full tablet breakpoint system. The content is centered and capped at a readable max width, which is acceptable, but the screen is essentially a scaled-up phone wizard and the native stack header shows the raw route pattern "audit/[placeId]" instead of the place/step title. Visual hierarchy and contrast within the card are solid.

critical_issues.location: Native stack header bar (both images, top) vs app/_layout.tsx:1384 and app/audit/[placeId]/[step].tsx:231-243
critical_issues.issue: The header title reads the literal route pattern "audit/[placeId]" instead of the intended place name / step title. The screen builds a custom headerTitle via YeeStackHeaderTitle (step.tsx:235-241) with stackHeaderOptions setting headerShown:true, but the root Stack registers the route with headerShown:false (app/_layout.tsx:1384). The visible result is an unstyled default header echoing the unresolved dynamic segment, which looks broken and gives no wayfinding (no place, no "Step 3 of 9" in the bar).
critical_issues.evidence: both images show 'audit/[placeId]' in the header; app/_layout.tsx:1384 `<Stack.Screen name="audit/[placeId]" options={{ headerShown: false }} />` conflicts with step.tsx:233 spreading stackHeaderOptions (headerShown:true) and a custom headerTitle
critical_issues.fix: Resolve the header ownership: either drop headerShown:false on the audit route in app/_layout.tsx so the per-screen Stack.Screen headerTitle (YeeStackHeaderTitle) wins, or ensure the [step].tsx Stack.Screen options actually override the parent. Confirm headerTitle renders YeeStackHeaderTitle with headerLabels.primary/secondary so the bar shows the place name and step instead of the raw segment.

improvements.location: app/audit/[placeId]/[step].tsx:423-507 (single KeyboardAwareScrollView column) and getResponsiveContentContainerStyle usage at 434-437
improvements.suggestion: On a large Android tablet the audit wizard is a single centered column; the spare horizontal width is only converted into gutters (getResponsiveContentContainerStyle / getAdaptiveHorizontalPadding in lib/responsive-layout.ts:662-673). Consider a tablet-only two-pane layout: persistent step navigator / progress rail on the left (the layout tokens already expose supportRailWidth and twoPaneGap in lib/responsive-layout-tokens.ts:818-845) and the question cards on the right, or a two-column grid of SelectionButton question cards. This better uses the canvas and reduces vertical scrolling on a domain with many rows.
improvements.evidence: step.tsx renders one YStack/scrollview column with no layout.isTablet branch; responsive-layout-tokens.ts:818 defines supportRailWidth/twoPaneGap that this screen never reads

improvements.suggestion: Single-choice answer options (Yes/No, Poor/Acceptable/Great) stack full-bleed across the entire content width, so short labels like 'No?' span the whole card. On tablet, lay short option sets in a horizontal row or 2-up grid so the choice group reads as a compact control rather than a tall stack, tightening the vertical rhythm.
improvements.evidence: 09-audit-domain-questions.png shows 'Poor?/Acceptable?/Great?' and 'Yes/No' each on its own full-width row; OptionGrid maps options into a vertical YStack gap=$2 (step.tsx:1255-1270) with no tablet row variant

improvements.location: StepHeader step pill row (step.tsx:669-703); visible in 08-audit-domain.png
improvements.suggestion: The nine step pills wrap onto two rows with minWidth:108 (step.tsx:686). On a tablet they could sit on a single horizontal scroll row or, better, become the left rail navigator. As-is they consume significant vertical space above the actual questions.
improvements.evidence: 08-audit-domain.png shows pills wrapping (Context/Weighting/Access on row 1, Activity Spaces/Amenities/... on rows 2-3); flexWrap='wrap' at step.tsx:669

tamagui_notes: This route hand-rolls every surface inline (Card, QuestionCard, SectionIntroCard, SelectionButton, CommentField, NoticeCard, SectionProgressCard) with designSystem.* tokens instead of the shared ui/* primitives; PACK declares design_system_components_used: (none). The shared Card (components/ui/Card.tsx), Field/FieldInput (components/ui/Field.tsx), ProgressBar (components/ui/ProgressBar.tsx) and Notice/Error states exist and cover most of these. Reusing them would unify radii/padding (the local Card uses radii.xl + p=$4 while ui/Card uses radii.lg) and reduce drift.
SelectionButton is intentionally an XStack-not-Button (documented at step.tsx:1284-1286 to allow label wrapping). The comment is grounded, so this is a reasonable deviation rather than an oversight.

step.tsx imports `designSystem` (the static light token set, lib/design-system.ts:453) rather than the live useDesignSystem hook, so this screen does not react to dark-mode/dyslexic/font-scale preferences the rest of the app honors (e.g. ui/Card, YeeStackHeaderTitle all use useDesignSystem). For a light-theme capture it looks correct, but it is a theming inconsistency.

The fixed FooterNav (step.tsx:1667-1768) uses layout.screenPaddingHorizontal for its padding but the scroll content uses getResponsiveContentContainerStyle's adaptive gutters; on a wide tablet the footer buttons stretch edge-to-edge while the content column is centered, so the Back/Save/Next row is not aligned with the card column above it.
platform_notes: Android nav: the app uses bottom tabs at the app root (app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx) but this audit route is a pushed stack screen, so no nav-rail-vs-bottom-nav concern applies here; the screen is a full-screen wizard.

lib/system-bars.ts hides the Android navigation bar (useHiddenAndroidNavBar in app/_layout.tsx:1295); the footer uses insets.bottom + 12 (step.tsx:1680) so the action row should clear the gesture area. The capture does not show a system nav bar, consistent with the hidden-nav-bar behavior.
Tap targets: SelectionButton rows use py=$3 px=$3.5 plus wrapping text, and footer Buttons inherit Tamagui Button height; both visibly exceed the 48dp Android minimum in the captures.
iOS-ported affordances: option rows are checkbox/radio-style full-width rows (not iOS chevrons or sheets), which is acceptable on Android; nothing obviously iOS-only is ported here.
Status bar shows 10:05 and system icons rendering over the cream background with dark content (StatusBar style 'dark' at app/_layout.tsx:1369), which reads correctly in light theme.
not_assessable: Exact device px width / which tablet tier (isNarrowTablet vs isWideTablet) this capture used — the screenshot is downscaled, so I cannot confirm the precise contentMaxWidth/gutter values from createResponsiveLayoutTokens.

Whether the header-pattern title is the native default header (parent Stack) or a momentary state during navigation — settling this needs a runtime check of which Stack.Screen options win for audit/[placeId].
Dark theme, font-scale, and dyslexic-font rendering (only the light capture was provided).
Exact WCAG contrast ratios; the primary-green selected rows (white text on #10231F) and body text on cream appear comfortably above AA but were not measured.
Runtime states: validation alerts (confirmStepProgress), saving spinner, offline NoticeCard, and the condition follow-up animation are not shown.
score_rationale: Usable with clear problems. Typography, spacing, contrast, and tap targets within the card column are solid (7-8 quality), but the screen does not adapt to the large Android tablet canvas (single centered column, no rail/grid despite available tokens) and the navigation header shows the raw route pattern 'audit/[placeId]' instead of a resolved title, which reads as broken wayfinding. These pull it to the middle of the 5-6 band.
